in_hebrew.name: הושענה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: הושענה היא שם שמשמעותו 'עזרה' ו'שבח' לאל. נמצא בברית החדשה, בספר הבשורה על-פי יוחנן, 12:13, 19:15, 19:17. נוצר על ידי הושע, הנביא. השם נושא חשיבות רבה בנצרות, ומרמז לעזרת האל ולשבח של האדם. השם נמשך מהעברית הקדם-כנענית, ומאוחר יותר נכנס ללשון העברית התלמודית.

in_greek.name: Ὑψίσαν
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὑψίσαν ἐστὶ ὄνομα τοῦ κυρίου, ὅ ἐστι ὑψηλότερος πάντων. Τὸ ὄνομα Ὑψίσαν συνδεόμενον ἐστὶ μὲ τὸν ὕψιστον θεόν. Ὑψίσαν ἐκφράζεται ἐν τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ ὡς Ὑשע, καὶ ἐν τῇ Ἑλληνίδι διαλέκτῳ ὡς Ὑψίσαν. Τὸ ὄνομα Ὑψίσαν συνδεόμενον ἐστὶ μὲ τὸν ὑψηλότερον θεόν. Ἡ ἀρχαία Ἑλληνικὴ διαλέκτος, ὑποστηρίζει, ὅτι Ὑψίσαν ἐστὶ ὄνομα τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψηλοτάτου.

in_latin.name: Hosannah
in_latin.long_meaning: Hosannah est nomen Domini, quod significat salutem, laudem, et honorem Deo. In Bibliis Novis, in Evangelio secundum Ioannem, 12:13, 19:15, 19:17, hoc nomen invenitur. Creavit propheta Hosea. Hosannah est nomen gravitas in Ecclesia Christiana, et designat auxilium Dei et laudem hominum. Nomen deductum est a lingua Hebraica antiqua et postea in lingua Hebraica Talmudica.

in_english.name: Hosannah
in_english.meaning: Salvation, praise, and honor to God
in_english.long_meaning: Hosannah is a name of the Lord, which means salvation, praise, and honor to God. It is found in the New Testament, in the Gospel of John, 12:13, 19:15, 19:17. It was created by the prophet Hosea. The name has great significance in the Christian Church, and it designates the aid of God and the praise of man. The name is derived from the ancient Hebrew language and later entered the Hebrew Talmudic language.

biblical_reference.note: The name Hosannah is used in the New Testament to express praise and glory to God.

saint_reference.note: Not a name of a saint, but a name of the Lord.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Hosannah" has become a popular exclamation of praise and joy in Judeo-Christian traditions, particularly during religious celebrations and processions. Its use can be traced back to the Old Testament, where it is mentioned in the Psalms and the prophetic books, imploring God for salvation and deliverance. Today, it is commonly chanted or sung in Christian worship services during the commemoration of Palm Sunday. The word "Hosannah" itself is derived from the Hebrew words "hashemeh rabbah," which means "save now, I pray," or "gracious Savior," emphasizing the plea for divine intervention and human need for redemption.
data.spiritual_significance: At its core, the cry of "Hosannah" holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, as it underscores their belief in the role of God as their ultimate savior. The use of "Hosannah" as a cry of praise and supplication reverberates the plea for salvation from sin and promises of the Messiah and the Kingdom of God. The expression's understanding as pleading for God's gracious intervention has become a crucial aspect of Christian faith, reflecting their dependence on the power and love of God. This prayer-like exclamation also represents hope, joy, and triumph, as associated with the entry of Jesus Christ into Jerusalem on Palm Sunday, heralding His eventual sacrifice and resurrection.

historical_references.reference: Hosanna, which means 'save us,' was the cry of the Jerusalem crowd as they welcomed Jesus into the city during the Triumphal Entry on Palm Sunday.
historical_references.context: Jesus' entry into Jerusalem before his crucifixion

historical_references.reference: The word 'Hosanna' is also used in the Old Testament Book of Psalms (118:25-26) as a shout of praise and triumph during a procession to the Temple.

trends: widespread use as a term of praise, often shouted or sung, particularly during religious processions or services.
platforms: Religious services (Christian, Jewish, etc.), Processions (Palm Sunday processions), and Music (hymns, praise songs)
modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Hosannah' is most commonly associated with its usage in religious contexts, particularly during Christian and Jewish services. It is often shouted or sung as a term of praise and is commonly used during Palm Sunday processions. The word 'Hosanna' comes from the Hebrew word 'hosheanah,' which means 'save us.' Today, it is also widely used in music, particularly in hymns and praise songs, as a term of worship and adoration.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Hosannah from London, United Kingdom embodies the meaning of Hosannah - "Save us, we pray!". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Hosannah means "save us, we pray" in Hebrew. It is a cry of praise and triumph, often used during the entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, symbolizing the people's longing for salvation and their recognition of God's power and sovereignty.
